answer: Sequential Work Witness. Each identity must solve a distinct, randomly assigned task whose answer is checkable and whose issuance rate is capped per falcon-class hardware profile, forcing real compute-time. A vertex in a task-dependency graph is only credited if its parent was solved within a fixed window, so parallel farming stalls. Attacker cost is wall-clock latency plus idle hardware: spinning N identities multiplies sequential delay, and the horizon for credential expiry stays short, forcing continuous fresh work to hold standing.
